next_step.guide: Before the interview, help the learner turn his three questions into open ones, and agree a quiet signal for “ask the next one” so you can sit in without taking over.
next_step.learner: Write your three questions and pick the one whose answer you most want to hear.

reach.alone: Ask a prepared question and write the answer down in his own words.
reach.with_help: With a guide nearby, follow a live thread the grandparent opens instead of rushing to the next question.
reach.not_yet: Running a long unscripted interview and shaping a full local history in one sitting — keep it to three questions today.

signals.watch: whether he follows a thread the grandparent opens
signals.looks_like: he pauses his list and asks “what was that like?”
signals.not: a judgement that he is or is not “a natural interviewer”

then.note: let the guide decide whether to nudge the live thread

signals.watch: whether a question drew a story or a number
signals.looks_like: “how many shops” got a count; “what did the street look like” got a scene
signals.not: a verdict that a question the learner wrote is “wrong”

then.note: offer an open rephrasing as one way

signals.looks_like: he marks a told-to-them memory as firsthand
signals.not: a conclusion that he “can’t tell sources apart” as a trait

companion_may.move: offer an open rephrasing of a question the learner wrote
companion_may.ceiling: suggest wording only; the learner keeps or changes it, and the companion never asks the question for him

companion_may.move: surface to the guide when a thread opens mid-interview
companion_may.ceiling: raise it quietly to the guide; never interrupt the grandparent or redirect the learner

guide_only.reserved: reading the room during the interview — letting a silence run when a memory wants more
guide_only.why: only a person present can feel when to wait, and that judgement is the heart of the session

guide_only.reserved: deciding which memories are the family’s to share and which to leave
guide_only.why: a consent and care judgement no file or service should make for a family

guide_only.reserved: choosing which plain spoken line to keep exactly as it was said
guide_only.why: hearing the one vivid line and building the passage around it is a human ear’s work

techniques.move: turn one session into a real interview the learner conducts, then shape the answers into a first page of local history
techniques.concept: history as a real person’s firsthand account, handled like a source
techniques.stuck_signature: treats history as dates and names and cannot see it as something that happened to actual people

services.for: turning the recorded interview into rough notes the learner can shape
services.boundary: transcribes only on request and keeps no copy of the audio or the text
services.offline_fallback: the learner takes written notes by hand during the interview

services.for: placing one remembered change on a before-and-after line in level three
services.boundary: renders only what the learner enters; makes no inference about the person
services.offline_fallback: draw the before-and-after line on paper

bundle.does: carries the whole session — the three questions, the source-sorting game, and the guide’s reserved work — in one file a person reads in full
bundle.cannot: cannot hear the interview as it happens or feel the silence that means a memory wants more; that catch stays with the guide

continuous.unlocks: could offer an open rephrasing in the moment a closed question lands flat
continuous.still_guide_only: reading the room and choosing which line to keep stay with the guide no matter the connection

record_hooks.writes: which source types the learner sorted confidently and which he rephrased, as behaviour

record_hooks.on: a missed source-sort in the game
record_hooks.writes: the specific source-handling slip, never a trait
